title: Private Camp Flex Mirror
oneLiner: A playful status mirror for parents to test whether elite camp spending is network-building, anxiety spending, or pure flex.

sourceSignals.signal: Some parents spend $20K+ on elite summer camps, framing them as networking and confidence investments.
A parent reports budgeting $3,600 for camp, then finding registration and materials fees that push the total higher.

stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web prototype for "Private Camp Flex Mirror", a playful status mirror for parents to test whether elite camp spending is network-building, anxiety spending, or pure flex. Target user: affluent or aspirational parents tempted by elite summer camp culture and worried about being left behind. Build the key UX around provocative tradeoff cards, a camp spend persona, and a shareable social-pressure receipt. Required UI sections: camp flex intake cards, network value meter, anxiety spend detector, parent persona result, and shareable receipt poster. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with a bold but readable composition, one memorable accent, and a strong shareable first impression without hiding the workflow. Use source signals S11 and S13 as problem evidence only.
